Stage 1 stays ticked, and its finding is kept in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`. Plan 4's Handoff reads `None`, so no entry needs amending first.

I have no tools this turn, so these are the calls I'll run next.

**1. Read before writing.** I need the Deferred-item schema, and I need to see whether the backlog file already exists so I append to it rather than overwrite it.

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/<deferred-backlog reference>
Read specs/deferred_items.md            # append only; create if absent
```

**2. Append four items** under one dated section. Below is a draft; I'll fit each item to the schema once I've read it.

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices for boat operators (roadmap Stage 2, O5). Email boat operators within an hour of a lock closing, by polling the closure log's live feed every 10 minutes. Text-message notices were out of scope.
      Size: small
      Done when: the notice job and the operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.
- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (O2). Run the Stage 1 closure-vs-gauge model daily on the river-level forecast. Stage 1 found closures under 2% of days below 3.1 m, rising to about 60% at 3.8 m (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md).
      Size: small; one 22-minute laptop fit, measured in Stage 1
      Done when: a 7-day outlook exists for each lock, with its result and measured run cost in a findings file.
- [ ] Per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks (O3). Stage 1 saw nearly the same curve at the four longest-record locks.
      Size: about 25 GB, 14× Stage 1's 1.8 GB
      Done when: curves for all 14 locks, with the measured run cost, are in a findings file.
- [ ] Closure-history map for the canal's boat operators (O4): one static map page.
      Size: about a day
      Done when: the map page shows each lock's closure history.
```

**3. Mark the roadmap and retire it.** First I add this line under the roadmap's title:

> PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Funding for the canal study ended; Stage 2 and Ranked-list items O2–O4 are in specs/deferred_items.md.

Then I move and commit it:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: 1 of 2 stages complete; defer Stage 2 and O2–O4"
```

This roadmap came from your own words, with no spec, so there are no methodology or critique files to retire with it. The commit stays local on `main`, and I won't push it.

After that the roadmap is closed, and no stage is handed off. If funding returns, `/deferred` will show the four items. Stage 1's findings file remains the starting point for O2 and O3.
